purpose: Run one final simulator-development refinement of the warm-start TriQTO candidate using a single predeclared late learning-rate reduction, then stop simulator hyperparameter tuning and proceed to a separately frozen exploratory IBM-hardware stage regardless of Step-10D outcome.

development_candidate.reason: Step 10D is not a second initialization comparison. It is a time-bounded final refinement of the reusable warm-start candidate before expiring QPU access. Step 10C found no statistically clear initialization winner, but warm-start had the higher frozen primary outer point estimate, converged earlier, and preserves the project checkpoint-reuse policy.

training.domain_schedule: equal optimizer-block count from original and bridge per epoch; shorter block list cycles deterministically

lr_schedule_rationale.epoch_1_to_20_3e_4: Retains the already demonstrated stable Step-10B/10C early optimization regime unchanged through the former Step-10B ceiling.
lr_schedule_rationale.epoch_21_to_40_1e_4: Reduces the late parameter-step scale by exactly 3x to test a single refinement hypothesis after Step 10C showed continued training-loss reduction, oscillatory late selection BA, and 100 percent clipping at norm 1.0.
lr_schedule_rationale.why_not_2e_4: A 1.5x reduction is intentionally not tested because this is not an LR sweep and may be too small to create a cleanly distinct refinement regime.
lr_schedule_rationale.why_not_3e_5_or_lower: A 10x-or-greater reduction risks effectively freezing a model that still showed development-selection headroom.
lr_schedule_rationale.claim: The values are a conservative predeclared engineering hypothesis, not a claim that 1e-4 is theoretically optimal.

selection.retention_reference: matching-seed Step-9A warm-start epoch-0 original-domain selection metrics
eligibility: original mechanism balanced accuracy >= matching-seed epoch-0 original mechanism BA - 0.02
original effect balanced accuracy >= matching-seed epoch-0 original effect BA - 0.02
eligible_checkpoint_order: minimum(original mechanism BA, bridge mechanism BA)

candidates: frozen Step-10C warm-start ensemble re-evaluated on the same development selection cohorts
Step-10D warm-start ensemble selected by the frozen per-seed selection rule
step10d_becomes_primary_if: all three Step-10D selected checkpoints satisfy the frozen per-seed original-retention eligibility rule
Step-10D ensemble satisfies the same 0.02 original-domain retention tolerance relative to the Step-9A epoch-0 ensemble
Step-10D bridge selection mechanism BA exceeds re-evaluated Step-10C warm bridge selection mechanism BA by more than 0.0005

outer_and_qpu_boundary.next_stage_after_step10d: separately frozen exploratory IBM hardware transfer pilot
outer_and_qpu_boundary.if_simulator_full_gate_remains_unmet: hardware stage must be labeled exploratory hardware-transfer validation under an incompletely satisfied simulator gate

hard_stop_after_step10d.exception: Only a code-integrity or execution-invalidating defect discovered before hardware may be repaired; such a repair must not be used to introduce a new scientific tuning intervention.

scientific_boundaries: Step 10D is development-only and makes no fresh outer-validation claim.
The spent Step-10C outer cohort is not read, materialized, scored, or used for selection in Step 10D.
The only change to the Step-10C warm-start optimization trajectory is LR=3e-4 for epochs 1-20 and LR=1e-4 for epochs 21-40.
Step 10D is the final simulator-development intervention before IBM hardware regardless of whether its development metric improves.
No QPU result may be used to tune Step 10D, choose a different simulator checkpoint after seeing hardware, or retroactively relax the Step-10C BA>=0.80 gate.
If the frozen simulator gate remains unmet, subsequent hardware results are exploratory transfer evidence rather than confirmatory proof of the full TriQTO hypothesis.
